traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 97 Tamaricaceae: shrubs or trees with slender branches and small, scale-like, alternate leaves; no stipules; flowers very small, regular, usually bisexual, in slender catkin-like spikes or racemes (alone in Reaumuria); sepals 4 to 6, petals as many, free; stamens 5 to 10; ovary superior; fruit a capsule, the seeds tufted with hairs.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Family file kept: tiny undivided scale or awl leaves (FNA and FOC read read 2026-10-19 agree).

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of China vol. 13, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers usually in racemes or panicles, rarely solitary (Reaumuria); FNA vol. 6: simple or compound racemes.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of China vol. 13, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs, subshrubs or trees; FNA vol. 6: shrubs or trees (subshrubs outside the flora).

traits.life_span.note: Flora of China vol. 13, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): woody shrubs and trees.

traits.growth_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 6, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs or trees, usually halophytes, rheophytes or xerophytes; shrub as the usual form.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 6, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves alternate; FOC: alternate.

traits.leaf_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 6, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves scale-like (subulate outside the flora), small; FOC: small, mostly scale-like, mostly with salt-secreting glands.

traits.stipules.note: Flora of North America vol. 6, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stipules absent; FOC: estipulate.

traits.sexual_system.note: Flora of China vol. 13, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers usually hermaphroditic; FOC Tamarix: rarely unisexual.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Flora of China vol. 13, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers regular.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of China vol. 13, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): calyx 4- or 5-fid, persistent; petals 4 or 5, free.

traits.perianth_fused.note: Flora of China vol. 13, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals free.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of China vol. 13, Tamarix (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers 4- or 5(or 6)-merous; family: calyx 4-5-fid, petals 4 or 5.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of China vol. 13, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens 4, 5 or more, inserted on the disk; Hutchinson's 5-10 kept as the span.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 6, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pistil (2-)3-4(-5)-carpellate; FOC: 2-5 carpels.

traits.ovary_position.note: Flora of China vol. 13, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): ovary superior, 1-loculed.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 6, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits capsular, loculicidal; FOC: capsule conic.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of China vol. 13, Tamaricaceae (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): calyx persistent.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.shape.templ.note: Flora of North America vol. 6, Tamaricaceae (read 2026-10-19): leaves alternate, scale-like, sessile, on slender green branchlets, many of which fall with the leaves in autumn. Drawing them as branchlet cards is the model's choice, as cedars' sprays are.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.shape.angle.note: Flora of North America vol. 6, Tamarix (read 2026-10-19): leaves scale-like, clasping or sheathing at the base. The 20 degrees, the least a sprig card allows, is the model's.

rules.generator.defaults.leaf_size.note: How PlantGen sizes a scale-leaved shrub's card (Caryophyllales families, 2026-10-19): as one deciduous branchlet. With a 3.5 mm card, saltcedar's first render grew over 2,000,000 attraction points and stopped.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.template.why: A tamarisk's scale leaves stand close along slender branchlets that fall whole, so a leaf card holds a branchlet, not one scale.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.angle.why: Scale leaves clasp the branchlet, their tips only a little free of it, at the least angle a sprig card draws.

generator.defaults.leaf_size.why: A card is one branchlet, as long as the branchlets are; a 3 mm scale on its own card spaced the shoots 2 cm apart and the crown never finished growing.
